targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: V3-EXQ-848 (ARC-005 TRACK A, successor to V3-EXQ-802's confounded joint-4-channel ladder): decouples the ladder to vary ONLY channels 1 (5-HT rigidity) and 2 (phasic-burst temperature) -- the two channels architecturally capable of reaching E3's precision readout -- while holding channels 3/4 (occupancy-only) fixed at L0 defaults, correctly excluded a priori. Applies a genuine substrate fix for channel 1 (SD-057 L7 dACC-consume bug, reading a collapsed proposer state; FIXED this session) for its first honest test. Result: C_precision_monotonicity FAILS (4/10 units satisfied vs 7/10 required), and the result is NOT the pre-registered-as-expected clean near-zero null (802's own finding was bit-identical rho=0.0 across all units) -- per-unit rho scatters widely (-0.5 to 0.866), correctly self-routing 'mixed' (some real but sub-threshold trend) rather than 'non_contributory' (clean expected null) per the driver's own pre-registered outcome map. Concur with self-route. FLAG FOR FUTURE REDESIGN: the per-unit criterion uses only 3 ladder levels (L0/L1/L2), and Spearman rho over 3 points is a coarse statistic that can swing to |rho|>=0.6 under pure noise alone -- this run's scattered (not uniformly near-zero) result is consistent with EITHER a genuine weak/inconsistent effect OR pure noise at this resolution, and the two are not well-discriminated by a 3-point correlation. Both pre-registered mechanistic explanations for channel 1/2's expected weakness remain intact and unaffected by this result: channel 1's dacc_adapter is confirmed untrained on non-degenerate goal_proximity inputs (a genuine substrate/training gap, Track C in the driver's own docstring, not yet in substrate_queue.json), and channel 2 remains architecturally inert under ~97%-committed normal operation (Track B, an uncommitted-only regime test, not yet queued).

recommended_substrate_queue_entry.title: Train dacc_adapter on non-degenerate use_mech_consume goal_proximity signals (ARC-005 Track C)
recommended_substrate_queue_entry.implementation_hint: V3-EXQ-848 confirmed dacc_adapter's response to a genuine post-fix candidate_goal_proximity signal is ~1e-8 in scale, 4-7 orders of magnitude below the ~0.87 scale of other dACC score_bias components -- consistent with dacc_adapter never having been trained on non-degenerate values of this input (use_mech_consume has never been ON in any prior training run). Build a training regime (or online-training exposure) that lets dacc_adapter learn to respond to real goal_proximity variation, then re-run V3-EXQ-848's channel-1 axis to give it an honest post-training test.

failure_record_entry.metric: dacc_adapter response magnitude to genuine goal_proximity input, ~1e-8 vs ~0.87 scale of other score_bias components
failure_record_entry.target: response magnitude within 1-2 orders of magnitude of other score_bias components after training exposure

learning_extracted: A correctly-scoped successor that decouples a confounded joint-ladder design (802's 4-channel yoke) into only the mechanistically-relevant channels is a strong methodology pattern -- it converted an uninterpretable confound into a clean, mechanistically-grounded result.

A driver that pre-registers the mechanistic reasons a null is EXPECTED (untrained consumer, architectural argmax-invariance) makes a null result a confirmation rather than a surprise -- but this run's actual finding (noisy/scattered, not clean-zero) is subtly different from what was pre-registered, and that difference is itself worth noting rather than smoothing into the expected bucket.

A per-unit Spearman rho over only 3 ladder levels is a coarse, high-variance statistic -- future redesigns wanting a cleaner discrimination between 'weak real effect' and 'noise' should consider more ladder levels (5+) rather than more seeds at 3 levels.
The dacc_adapter undertraining gap (Track C) was diagnosed with a specific quantified magnitude (~1e-8 vs ~0.87) but had no substrate_queue.json entry -- now created.
